faq.a: Click Add to Server at the top of this page (or /invite), pick your server, and authorize. You need Manage Server permission in that server. Then run /setup in the server and open the dashboard to configure it.
faq.q: How do I add the bot to my server?

faq.a: Every slash-command reply is ephemeral by design — only you can see it, so command spam never clutters the channel. The only public posts are the ones a command is meant to make in a channel: poll embeds, announcements, suggestions, FAQ replies, starboard posts, and trade proposals.
faq.q: Why are all command replies only visible to me?

faq.a: An admin runs /ticket-setup in the channel for the ticket panel. Members click the button to open a ticket; staff use /ticket-claim, /ticket-add, /ticket-remove, and /ticket-close. Category, log channel, and support role live on the dashboard Tickets tab.
faq.q: How do I set up tickets?

faq.a: An admin runs /application-create (name, description, up to 5 questions) then /application-open. Members apply with /apply; staff review with /application-list, /application-view, /application-accept, and /application-deny. See the Applications guide above.
faq.q: How do I set up applications?

faq.a: An admin runs /stream-add for a Twitch or YouTube streamer (or adds them on the dashboard Streams tab) and picks an announcement channel. The bot posts when they go live. Use /stream-template to rename a channel while someone is live — see the Streams guide above.
faq.q: How do I set up streams?

faq.a: Leveling runs automatically: members earn XP from chatting and commands. Check progress with /rank, see the top 10 with /leaderboard, and set levels with /setlevel (admin). Level-up messages and level roles are on the dashboard Leveling tab.
faq.q: How do I set up leveling?

faq.a: Invite tracking is automatic once the bot has Manage Server permission — it compares its cached invite list to the live list on every join to find the inviter. See stats with /invites and /inviteleaderboard, details with /invite-info, and reset with /invite-reset (admin). The fake-account age threshold is on the dashboard Invites tab.
faq.q: How do I set up invites?

faq.a: In MySQL, per-server: every row carries a guild_id, so no server can see or affect another server's data. That covers settings, tickets, applications, economy balances and inventories, starboard posts, message logs, polls, and bot-tracking flags.
faq.q: Where is my data stored?

faq.a: The bot backs up the whole database every day at 3 AM (configurable) and keeps the last 30 days. The owner can run one on demand with /backup, and staff can see backup files and the run log on the Staff → Backups page. Restore with: node scripts/restore-db.js <file> --confirm.
faq.q: How do backups work?

faq.a: Every error and warning the bot hits is written to the MySQL error_logs table and to logs/bot-errors.log on the host. Staff can browse them on the Staff → Errors page or with /errors, and read one in full with /error <id>.
faq.q: How do I report an error / where do errors go?

faq.a: Run /stream-template set with a template that contains {name} (you can also use {game} and {title}), max 100 characters — or set it on the dashboard Streams tab, which shows a live preview. The channel renames when a streamer goes live and restores its original name when they go offline.
faq.q: How do I change the live-channel name template?

faq.a: On the host: git pull (and npm install if package.json changed), then npm run deploy to re-register the slash commands, then restart the bot (npm start, or your process manager). The current version and what changed are on the /version page.
faq.q: How do I update the bot?
How do I set up verification?
faq.a: An admin runs /verify-setup with a channel, the role to grant, and a mode — Button or Captcha (a quick math question in a modal). New members are DM'd where to verify. Toggle it with /verify-toggle, or use the dashboard Verification tab.

faq.q: How does counting work?
faq.a: An admin runs /counting-setup with the channel. Each message there must start with the next number. A wrong number or the same person counting twice in a row deletes the message and resets the count to 0. /counting-reset resets it manually.

faq.q: How do bump reminders work?
faq.a: An admin runs /bump-setup with the reminder channel. When someone types !d bump (or DISBOARD confirms a bump), the bot posts a 'Time to bump!' reminder 2 hours later. /bump shows the timer; /bump record records a manual bump.

faq.q: How do temporary voice channels work?
faq.a: Set a 'create' voice channel and a category on the dashboard Temp VC tab. Joining the create channel makes a personal voice channel named after you; it is deleted when empty. Owners manage theirs with /tempvc (limit, lock, unlock, rename, kick, claim).

faq.q: Can I play Spotify links?
faq.a: Yes — /play accepts a Spotify track link and matches the track on YouTube. Spotify audio is never streamed directly (there is no public Spotify audio API), so this is a lookup. Playlist and album links only match their top YouTube result.

faq.q: How do I set up birthdays?
faq.a: An admin runs /birthday-setup with the announcement channel and the hour (default 9 AM, bot host local time). Members set theirs with /birthday set (month, day, optional year). The bot posts a birthday embed once per user per year.

faq.q: Why can't I take a reaction role?
faq.a: That role may have requirements: a role you must already have, a minimum number of days in the server, or a minimum leveling level. The bot tells you exactly which requirement you missed. Admins set requirements with /reactionroles-add.

faq.q: How does the weather command work?
faq.a: /weather <city, ZIP, or "lat,lon"> shows current conditions from Open-Meteo (free, no API key). /forecast shows up to 7 days ahead. An admin can set a server default location and units with /weather-set — imperial (°F/mph) by default, metric (°C/km/h) if set.

faq.q: How do saved music playlists work?
faq.a: Use /playlist save while music is playing to save the current queue under a name, then /playlist load to queue it back. Playlists are per-user and per-server — max 10 per user, 50 tracks each.

faq.q: How does the daily trivia work?
faq.a: An admin sets it up with /trivia-daily setup (channel + hour, UTC). The bot posts one question per day; the first correct answer wins 50 coins and a trivia point. Play with /trivia-daily play.

faq.q: How does a heist work?
faq.a: Run /heist with a bet (50–5000 coins). A 60-second lobby opens and others can join. Success chance is 40% plus 10% per extra crew member (max 90%). Success pays everyone their bet back x2; failure loses the bet.

faq.q: What are member milestones?
faq.a: When the server hits 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, or 10000 members, the bot celebrates in the milestone channel and the member who triggered it earns 100 coins. Set the channel with /milestone-setup.

faq.q: What is a role menu?
faq.a: A select-menu message where members pick roles from a dropdown — select again to remove. Admins build them with /rolemenu create and /rolemenu add. Reaction-role requirements apply.

faq.q: How does auto-translate work?
faq.a: Admins pick channels with /translate-setup and a target language. Messages in other languages there get an automatic translation reply. It uses Google's free unofficial translate endpoint (no key, no SLA), and /translate translates any text on demand.

faq.q: What is DJ mode?
faq.a: DJ mode locks the music control commands — /skip, /stop, /pause, /resume, /filter, /queue-clear — to a DJ role (and admins). An admin enables it with /dj-setup or on the dashboard Music tab. /play, /queue, /lyrics and /nowplaying stay open to everyone while "gate only control commands" is on.

faq.q: How do countdowns work?
faq.a: An admin runs /countdown create with a title and a time like "in 2h30m" or "2026-12-25 18:00". The bot posts an embed that updates every minute (every 5 minutes while more than a day is left), and when it hits zero it edits the message to "🎉 <title> is here!" and pings the channel once.

faq.q: What does prestiging do?
faq.a: At the max level (100 by default) a member can /prestige to reset to level 1 and gain +1 prestige. Each prestige gives a permanent +10% XP multiplier (cap +100% at prestige 10), a ⭐ badge on /rank, and a permanent prestige role if the server configured one.

faq.q: Can I have more than one ticket panel?
faq.a: Yes — /ticket-panel create posts a new panel with its own category, staff role and topic. /ticket-setup stays as the default panel, and tickets record which panel they came from.

faq.q: How do invite-based auto-roles work?
faq.a: An admin maps an invite code to a role with /inviterole add. Anyone who joins through that invite automatically gets the role — it's based on the invite code used, not who invited them. The code must be a real active invite in the server.

faq.q: How does 24/7 music mode work?
faq.a: An admin runs /247 enable and picks a voice channel. The bot stays in that channel around the clock — even with an empty queue — and rejoins if it gets disconnected or kicked. /247 disable turns it off. The toggle is also on the dashboard Music tab.

faq.q: Can someone steal my economy coins?
faq.a: Only from your wallet, with /rob — a 35% success chance, stealing 10–30% of your wallet (min 10, max 1,000 coins). Coins in your bank can never be robbed, so use /deposit to keep them safe. A failed robbery costs the robber a fine of up to 100 coins. Servers can turn robbery off entirely (dashboard Economy tab).

faq.q: How do work jobs work?
faq.a: Run /jobs to see your server's jobs — each has a payout range, an unlock cost, and a level requirement. Buy one with /job buy <name>, pick it with /job set <name>, and /work then pays from that job's range instead of the default 50–250 coins.

faq.q: How do giveaway bonus entries work?
faq.a: When a giveaway is created with a bonus role, holders of that role get extra entries (set at creation, default 1), and Nitro boosters get +1 automatically if the server has a booster role configured. The draw is weighted by total entries, so more entries means a better chance — but nobody can win twice in one draw.

faq.q: How do tempbans work?
faq.a: An admin runs /tempban @user 7d [reason] — the member is banned and automatically unbanned when the duration ends (checked every 5 minutes). /tempban-list shows active tempbans; /tempban-cancel unbans early. You can't tempban the server owner, yourself, or anyone with a higher role than you. The Moderation tab on the dashboard lists active tempbans with cancel buttons.

faq.q: How do I delete messages from one user, or messages containing certain text?
faq.a: Use /purge <amount> [user] [contains] — it deletes up to 100 recent messages matching the filters. Pinned messages and messages older than 14 days are skipped and counted (Discord won't bulk-delete those). /clear still deletes an unfiltered batch. Every purge is audit-logged.

faq.q: How does the lottery work?
faq.a: Buy one ticket per week with /lottery buy [numbers] (default 100 coins, 3 numbers 1-30 or random). The draw runs Sundays at 20:00 server time; the jackpot is 50% of the week's ticket sales, split between players matching all 3 numbers, and 2 matches pay 100 coins. Results post to the lottery channel and winners are DM'd. /lottery status shows the jackpot and time to draw.

faq.q: How do I set up server rules?
faq.a: An admin runs /rules-setup and picks a channel, then fills in the title and rules in the modal. /rules shows them to anyone; /rules-edit updates the posted message in place. There is only one rules message per server — re-running setup edits it. You can also edit rules on the dashboard General tab.

faq.q: What does anti-nuke protection do?
faq.a: It watches for bursts of destructive actions (channel/role deletes, mass bans/kicks) and, when one member passes the threshold (default 5 actions in 60 seconds), kicks, bans, or strips their roles, then alerts the owner. Set it up with /antinuke-setup or on the Staff → Anti-Nuke dashboard page. It can't prevent the first deletions — Discord's audit log, which it uses to identify who did it, can lag a few seconds.

faq.q: Can new members get a welcome DM?
faq.a: Yes — set the message with /welcome-dm set <message> (placeholders {user}, {username}, {server}) and toggle it with /welcome-dm toggle. If a member's DMs are closed the DM is skipped silently. The dashboard Welcome tab has the message field, toggle, and a test button that DMs you a preview.

gettingStarted.intro: Four steps and the bot is running in your server.

steps.body: Click the Add to Server button (top of this page, or /invite). Pick your server and authorize. You need Manage Server permission in that server. The bot asks for the permissions it needs to do its jobs (read/send messages, manage roles for auto-role and shop roles, manage channels for tickets and server stats).
steps.title: 1. Add the bot to your server

steps.body: If you host the bot yourself, the dashboard starts in setup-wizard mode on first run: open the one-time setup link it prints to the console (or in setup-token.txt) and walk through 8 steps — bot token, client ID, database, dashboard, API keys, backups. The wizard tests the bot token and the database connection before saving, and writes config.json for you. No manual file editing needed.
steps.title: 2. Run the first-run setup wizard

steps.body: Discord (required): https://discord.com/developers/applications — bot token + client ID. Twitch (stream alerts): https://dev.twitch.tv/console. YouTube (stream alerts + music search): https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/youtube.googleapis.com. Steam (profile lookups): https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey. Everything else works without a key.
steps.title: 3. Get API keys (only the ones you need)

steps.body: Run /setup in your server (sets the welcome channel, log channel, and ticket settings), then open the dashboard, pick your server, and work through the tabs — General, Moderation, Tickets, Streams, Leveling, and the rest. Every setting saves to the database and applies within a minute, no restart needed.
steps.title: 4. Configure your server

gettingStarted.title: Getting started

steps: An admin runs /ticket-setup in the channel where the ticket panel should live.
Members click the panel button to open a private ticket channel.
Support staff use /ticket-claim to take it, /ticket-add and /ticket-remove to manage who can see it, and /ticket-close to close it (a transcript is saved).
Ticket category, log channel, and support role are set on the dashboard Tickets tab (or with /setup).
guides.title: Tickets

steps: An admin runs /application-create with a name, a description, and up to 5 questions, then /application-open to accept applications.
Members apply with /apply and answer the questions in a modal.
Staff review with /application-list (pending counts), /application-view to read one, and /application-accept or /application-deny — accepting can grant a role and DMs the applicant.
Check your own applications anytime with /application-status. Manage forms on the dashboard Applications tab.
guides.title: Applications

steps: An admin runs /stream-add (Twitch or YouTube) and picks the announcement channel, or adds streamers on the dashboard Streams tab.
When a streamer goes live, the bot posts an announcement embed. /stream-announce posts one manually (handy for Facebook/TikTok).
To rename a channel while someone is live: /stream-template set with a template containing {name} (also {game} and {title}), max 100 characters — or set it on the Streams tab with the live preview.

The channel is renamed only on live/offline transitions, and restores its exact original name when the stream ends. Discord allows about 2 renames per 10 minutes per channel, so the bot queues retries instead of failing.
guides.title: Streams + live channel name

steps: An admin runs /welcome-setup with a channel and a message template — placeholders: {user}, {username}, {server}, {membercount}.
Turn them on/off with /welcome-toggle, and preview one with /welcome-test.
Goodbye messages work the same way: /goodbye-setup and /goodbye-toggle.
Both can also be configured on the dashboard Welcome tab, with a live preview as you type.
guides.title: Welcome messages

steps: An admin runs /automod-setup: spam limits (messages per window), what happens on spam (delete / warn / timeout), link and invite blocking, and the log channel.
Add banned words with /automod-words add, remove with /automod-words remove, list with /automod-words list.
Exempt roles or channels with /automod-exempt so staff and announcement channels are never filtered.
View current settings anytime with /automod. Everything is also on the dashboard Automod tab.
guides.title: Automod

steps: An admin runs /suggestions-setup with the channel suggestions go to.
Members submit with /suggest (title + details in a modal). The bot posts it with 👍 / 👎 voting — one vote per user.
Staff review with /suggest-status (your own) or the dashboard Suggestions tab, and Approve, Deny, or mark Implemented.
The suggester is told the outcome.
guides.title: Suggestions

steps: Everyone starts with 100 coins. Earn more with /daily (once a day, 100–500 coins plus a random daily item) and /work (once an hour, 50–250 coins).
Check your wallet and bank with /balance, move coins with /deposit and /withdraw, send coins with /pay, and see the richest members with /eco-leaderboard.
Spend in the shop: /shop lists items, /buy <id> buys (role items grant the role, everything else lands in /inventory). One item per guild per day is 25% off as the daily deal.

Crates (Common 500, Rare 1,500, Legendary 5,000) are opened with /open-crate for random loot. Sell items back with /sell (usually half price). Trade with another member using /trade — they accept, you confirm, and the swap happens in one database transaction.
Feeling lucky? /slots, /blackjack, /roulette, /gamble-coinflip, and /gamble-dice all use the same wallet. Minimum bet 10, maximum 10,000, 5 seconds between games.
guides.title: Economy, crates & trading

steps: An admin runs /starboard-setup with a channel and a threshold (default 3 stars).
When a message collects that many ⭐ reactions, the bot posts it to the starboard channel as an embed (author, content, jump link, star count, first image).
The count updates live as stars arrive. If it drops below the threshold, the starboard post is deleted.
Bot messages and messages already in the starboard channel are ignored.
guides.title: Starboard
Verification gate
steps: An admin runs /verify-setup with a channel, the role to grant, and a mode — Button (click to verify) or Captcha (click, then answer a quick math question in a modal).
The bot posts a Verify button panel in the channel and enables the gate. New members are DM'd where to verify.
Turn it on/off with /verify-toggle. Grants and failures are logged to the verification_logs table.
The same settings live on the dashboard Verification tab.

guides.title: Counting & bump reminders
steps: An admin runs /counting-setup with the counting channel. Each message there must start with the next number — a wrong number or the same person counting twice in a row deletes the message and resets the count to 0.
Correct counts get a ✅ reaction. Reset manually with /counting-reset.
For bumps, an admin runs /bump-setup with the reminder channel. When someone types !d bump (or DISBOARD confirms a bump), the bot waits 2 hours, then posts a 'Time to bump!' reminder.
Check the timer anytime with /bump, or record a manual bump with /bump record.

guides.title: Temporary voice channels
steps: Set the 'create' voice channel and a category on the dashboard Temp VC tab.
Joining the create channel spins up a personal voice channel named after you and moves you in. It is deleted when it becomes empty.
Owners manage theirs with /tempvc limit, /tempvc lock, /tempvc unlock, /tempvc rename, and /tempvc kick.
If the owner leaves, someone else in the channel can take over with /tempvc claim.

guides.title: Music, filters, lyrics & Spotify
steps: Join a voice channel, then /play <song name, YouTube URL, or Spotify track link>. Spotify links are matched on YouTube — Spotify audio is never streamed directly.
Control playback with /skip, /stop, /pause, /resume, and /queue. /nowplaying shows the current track with a progress bar.
Apply an audio filter with /filter (bassboost, nightcore, vaporwave, 8d, or off) — the current track restarts with the filter on, because filters need FFmpeg re-encoding.
Get lyrics with /lyrics (the song playing now, or /lyrics song: Artist - Title). Lyrics come from the free lyrics.ovh API — no key needed.

guides.title: Birthdays
steps: Members set their birthday with /birthday set (month, day, and an optional year for ages).
An admin runs /birthday-setup with the announcement channel and the hour (default 9 AM, bot host local time).
On the day, the bot posts a birthday embed once per user per year. See what's coming with /birthday list, or remove yours with /birthday remove.

guides.title: Reaction roles with requirements
steps: Create a panel with /reactionroles-setup, then add pairs with /reactionroles-add — optionally with a required role, a minimum days-in-server, and/or a minimum leveling level.
Members who miss a requirement get an ephemeral message naming exactly what they missed; members who meet them get the role as usual.
See every mapping and its requirements with /reactionroles-list, or on the dashboard Reaction Roles tab.

guides.title: Weather
steps: Check the weather anywhere with /weather <city, ZIP, or "lat,lon"> — temperature, feels-like, condition, humidity, wind, pressure, visibility, sunrise and sunset.
See ahead with /forecast <location> [days 1-7] — high/low, condition, and precipitation chance per day.
An admin can set a server default with /weather-set (location + imperial/metric units), so /weather with no location just works.
Weather comes from Open-Meteo — free, no API key needed.

guides.title: Saved music playlists
steps: While music is playing, run /playlist save with a name to save the current queue as a playlist.
Use /playlist load with the name (join a voice channel first) to queue the whole playlist back.
List your playlists with /playlist list, delete with /playlist delete, rename with /playlist rename. Max 10 playlists per user per server, 50 tracks each.
The dashboard Music tab lists every playlist in the server with a delete button.

guides.title: Daily trivia
steps: An admin runs /trivia-daily setup with a channel and an hour (UTC, default 12) — the bot posts one question per day there.
Members answer by clicking an answer button. The first correct answer wins 50 coins and a trivia point.
Anyone can play today's question with /trivia-daily play, and see the top players with /trivia-leaderboard.
The question is the same for the whole server each day, and comes from the bot's built-in trivia bank.

guides.title: Heist
steps: Run /heist with a bet (50–5000 coins from your wallet) to open a 60-second lobby.
Other members join with the Join button — success chance is 40% plus 10% per extra crew member (max 90%).
If the heist succeeds, everyone gets their bet back x2. If it fails, everyone loses their bet.
There is a 1-hour cooldown per user between heists.

guides.title: Member milestones
steps: An admin runs /milestone-setup with a channel for milestone celebrations.
When the server hits 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, or 10000 members, the bot posts a celebration embed there.
The member who triggers a milestone earns a 100-coin bonus. Each milestone only fires once.
Anyone can check the next milestone and progress with /milestones.

guides.title: Button role menus
steps: An admin runs /rolemenu create with a title (and optional channel) to post a menu message.
Add options with /rolemenu add (menu ID, role, label, optional emoji and description). A menu holds up to 25 options.
Members pick a role from the dropdown — selecting it again removes it. Reaction-role requirements (required role, days in server, level) apply.
Remove options with /rolemenu remove and delete the whole menu with /rolemenu delete.

guides.title: Auto-translate
steps: An admin runs /translate-setup with a channel and a target language — messages in that channel are auto-translated into it.
Translation uses Google's free unofficial endpoint (no key, no SLA) — if it fails, the message is simply left untranslated.
Anyone can translate text on demand with /translate and a target language code (e.g. es, fr, de).
Bot messages and commands are never translated.

guides.title: DJ mode
steps: An admin runs /dj-setup with a DJ role to turn DJ mode on — or picks the role and the toggle on the dashboard Music tab.
When DJ mode is on, only the DJ role (and admins) can use /skip, /stop, /pause, /resume, /filter and /queue-clear. Everyone else gets an error naming the DJ role.
With "gate only control commands" on (the default), /play, /lyrics, /queue and /nowplaying stay open to everyone. Turn it off and every music command needs the DJ role.
DJ mode can't be enabled without a DJ role set — the command and the dashboard both refuse with a clear error.

guides.title: Emoji manager
steps: An admin with Manage Emojis runs /emoji-add with a name and an image URL or attachment (PNG/JPG/GIF under 256KB, name 2–32 letters, numbers or underscores).
The bot checks the server's emoji slot limit first and errors clearly if the server is full.
/emoji-list shows the server's custom emoji (paginated), and /emoji-remove deletes one by name.
Additions and removals are logged to the database (emoji_logs). The dashboard Emojis tab has the same list, add and remove.

guides.title: Countdowns
steps: An admin or staff member runs /countdown create with a title and a time — "in 2h30m", "in 3d", or an absolute date like "2026-12-25 18:00".
The bot posts a countdown embed that updates itself — every minute once under 24h is left, every 5 minutes before that.
When it hits zero the message is edited to "🎉 <title> is here!" and the channel is pinged once.
/countdown list shows active countdowns; /countdown cancel removes one. The dashboard Events tab (Scheduled) has the same list with create/cancel.

guides.title: Prestige levels
steps: Members earn XP as usual up to the max level (100 by default, config.json leveling.maxLevel).
At max level, /prestige shows a confirm button — prestiging resets level to 1 and XP to 0, and grants +1 prestige.
Each prestige gives a permanent +10% XP multiplier, capped at +100% (prestige 10). A ⭐ badge shows on /rank and the rank card.
An admin can set a prestige role (dashboard Leveling tab or guild_settings prestige_role_id) that is granted permanently when a member prestiges. /prestige-leaderboard shows the top prestige users.

guides.title: Multiple ticket panels
steps: An admin runs /ticket-panel create with a title and a category — optionally a staff role, a channel to post in, and a description.
Each panel is separate: its own category, staff role and topic. /ticket-setup stays as the default/first panel.
Tickets opened from a panel record which panel they came from, so staff can tell which panel a ticket belongs to.
/ticket-panel list shows all panels; /ticket-panel delete removes one. The dashboard Tickets tab lists panels with create/delete.

guides.title: Invite-based auto-roles
steps: An admin runs /inviterole add with an invite code and a role — e.g. the "youtube" invite gets the "From YouTube" role.
When someone joins through that invite, the role is granted automatically. The role is based on the code used, not the inviter.
The code must be a real active invite in the server (checked on add) and the role must sit below the bot's highest role.
/inviterole list shows all rules; /inviterole remove deletes one. The dashboard Invites tab has the same list with add/remove.

guides.title: Work jobs & robbery
steps: Run /jobs to see your server's job catalog (Dishwasher, Barista, Mechanic, Developer by default).
Unlock a job with /job buy <name> (costs coins, needs the listed level), then pick it with /job set <name> — /work now pays that job's range.
Keep coins safe from /rob by moving them to the bank with /deposit — only wallet coins can be stolen.
Admins can turn robbery off for the whole server on the dashboard Economy tab.
